_comment: STARTER DATA — VERIFY BEFORE THE DEMO. South Florida invasive plants believed to be on the Florida Invasive Species Council (FISC) Category I list. Check every name, category and 'why' against the official FISC Invasive Plant List (https://floridainvasives.org/plant-list/) and the UF/IFAS Assessment of Non-native Plants (https://assessment.ifas.ufl.edu/) before relying on it. Synonyms are older or alternate names a model may return.

species.why: Forms dense thickets that crowd out mangroves, pinelands and Everglades natives across hundreds of thousands of acres.
Turned open Everglades sawgrass marsh into dense forest that soaks up water and burns intensely.
Shallow roots topple in hurricanes and block roads, and its litter erodes beaches where sea turtles nest.
Vines smother native trees, and every aerial 'potato' sprouts a new vine, so one plant can overrun a hammock.
Blankets Everglades tree islands and carries fire up into the canopy, killing the trees underneath.
Smothers forest understory and acts as a fire ladder into the treetops.
Floating mats clog canals and flood-control structures and starve the water of light and oxygen for fish.
Mats choke canals and flood-control gates and suffocate native aquatic life.
Fills lakes and canals from bottom to surface, slowing drainage and flood control.
Forms dense mats that crowd out natives and burn extremely hot, spreading wildfire.
Escapes from yards into mangroves and coastal hammocks, crowding out native trees.
Fast-growing tree that shades out native hammock and wetland plants.
Vines smother coastal hammocks and mangrove edges, and its seeds float to new shorelines.
Crowds out the native dune plants that hold sand, leaving beaches weaker against storm erosion.
Forms dense thickets in hammocks and Everglades tree islands that shade out native seedlings.
Forms dense thickets in hammocks that keep native trees from regrowing.
Takes over rare pine rocklands and burns hot, crowding out endangered native plants.
Turns wetlands and prairies into tallow forest and changes the soil and water chemistry around it.
Cross-breeds with Florida's rare native lantana, and its berries are toxic to pets and livestock.
Popular yard plant that escapes into wetlands and ditches, forming dense stands that crowd out natives.
Crowds out native coastal and mangrove plants along South Florida shorelines.
Carpets the ground and climbs hammock trees, shading out native plants.
